rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and map the full elution window without risking severe truncation. This gives a first look at overall retention, whether peaks are compressed at the front or tailing into the hold, and where to focus later refinements.

All compounds eluted within 10 min, so the issue is a single unresolved pair rather than retention. Doubling tG at the same phi window and temperature tests whether that pair is slope-responsive; if R(4,5) improves substantially, we can later shorten from there, and if not, we will know to change temperature or the phi window instead.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive, so move to an intermediate gradient time to seek the shortest fully resolved method while keeping the same broad window and temperature. Around tG 24 min should still keep all pairs at or near baseline resolution while reducing the time penalty versus 40 min.

The unresolved pair improves markedly with longer tG, and a simple interpolation from 24 to 40 min suggests full resolution may appear around 30 min while keeping the time penalty modest. This directly tests whether we can cross R = 1.5 close to the optimum runtime.

Since changing slope trades one critical pair against another, the next lever is temperature to alter selectivity rather than just gradient steepness. A lower temperature should increase retention slightly and may reorder or separate the close pairs enough to improve the resolution term while keeping t_last near the no-penalty region.

The 25 C run is already close to ideal, with only one pair just below full credit and only a small time penalty. Testing one temperature step upward may keep the improved selectivity while pulling t_last closer to 10 min, potentially raising CRF above the current best.

At 25 C only one pair is slightly below full credit, so a small increase in gradient time should lift that pair above R = 1.5 with only a modest added time penalty. This is the most direct move toward a fully resolved method near the current optimum.

The best run used a broader window than needed, with the first peak not appearing until 5.46 min. Raising phi0 one step should compress unproductive early time and may improve both runtime and selectivity around the lone sub-1.5 pair without sacrificing elution of the late peaks.

This is very close to ideal: one pair is just shy of full credit and t_last is essentially at 10 min. A small increase in tG should push the 3,4 pair above R = 1.5 while only modestly increasing runtime, which is the most likely route to CRF 1.0 or very near it.

The best method is almost perfect, so the remaining opportunity is to tighten the upper end of the gradient window while keeping tG at 20 min. Lowering phi1 one step may preserve separation but slightly delay the critical mid pair relative to the overall window in a favorable way, and it is a cleaner way to tune selectivity than adding time.

The fully resolved 0.90 endpoint improved over the 22 min run, so continue trimming the gradient window upward from the high-organic end. A slightly lower phi1 may keep all pairs resolved while bringing the last peak even closer to 10 min, which is the only remaining way to beat the current best if selectivity holds.

Lowering phi1 too far increased runtime, so the next promising refinement is to raise phi0 another step from the current best method. We have already reached the maximum CRF, so this injection should probe robustness and whether a narrower, more efficient window can preserve perfect performance. Raising phi0 one step tests how much front-end trimming is tolerated before the critical pair starts to lose resolution.

The higher phi0 still gives perfect separation with comfortable margin and a faster run, so the next optimization is to shorten tG by one step at the same window. This tests whether we can keep all pairs at R ≥ 1.5 while making the method even more efficient within the same maximum CRF.

The method remains perfect after trimming phi1 to 0.90, so test one further reduction in the upper endpoint at the same phi0 and tG. This checks whether the gradient window can be narrowed further while maintaining all pairs above R = 1.5 and keeping t_last under 10 min.

The full-resolution window still holds at phi1 = 0.85, so one more step lower will locate the upper-end boundary for a tightly focused method. This is a useful final robustness/optimization check because the critical pair margin has actually improved as phi1 decreased.
